glosses: to go numb, go to sleep
Provoquer la paralysie ou rendre insensible le corps ou une partie du corps.

examples.text: Le sommeil engourdit. — Il y a des venins, des plantes qui engourdissent.
Nous étions non pas las, mais notre cerveau était engourdi à la suite de la terrible tension d'esprit au milieu de la tempête. Pour ma part, j'avais la tête lourde.
Et, tournant à son tour les yeux vers la portière, il s'abîma dans une soudaine et muette rêverie. Le balancement de la voiture l'engourdissait.
Elle contempla longtemps, comme pour engourdir sa peine, le patient manège des abeilles qui s'affairaient d'une fleur à l'autre.
Mais ces mecs-là n'auraient quand même pas la prétention d'engourdir le pognon de ma nièce, non ?
À tout bout de champ, je portais la main sur le renflement provoqué par la liasse, craignant de me faire engourdir mon pognon.
Quand elle avait douze ans, sa maman, une Argentine volage, a joué cassos avec un beau ténébreux, en engourdissant un rude pacsif de dollars à son cornard.

examples.text: Um die Oberfläche bei Schnee und Eis abzustumpfen sind als Streumaterial Sand, Splitt und Granulat geeignet.

„Doch ich will weder abstumpfen noch mich in die bequeme Ohnmacht flüchten, sowieso nichts ändern zu können.“

„Der ORF will sein Publikum nicht durch ein Übermaß an Gewaltdarstellungen abstumpfen.“

„»Ich muss gestehen, dass ich nie besonders feste moralische Prinzipien hatte. Ich will mich nicht rechtfertigen, aber eine Erklärung dafür liegt in dem unaufhörlichen Überlebenskampf, den ich von frühester Kindheit an zu bestehen hatte. Dieser Kampf hat meine Skrupel abstumpfen lassen.«“

glosses: Physically unable to feel, not having the power of sensation.

examples.text: fingers numb with cold
legs numb from kneeling

glosses: Emotionally unable to feel or respond in a normal way.

examples.text: numb with shock; numb with boredom

[…] when we know that hundreds are rendered homeless every day, and countless thousands are killed and wounded, men and boys mowed down like a field of grain, and with as little compunction, we grow a little bit numb to human misery.
[…] seeing the dog—somehow that made me feel again. I’d been too dazed, too numb, to feel the full viciousness of it.
[…] he submitted […] as a traitor, his mind numb with vodka, submits to a firing squad.

[…] he did lap me
Even in his own garments, and gave himself,
All thin and naked to the numb cold night.

glosses: To cause to become numb (physically or emotionally).

examples.text: The dentist gave me novocaine to numb my tooth before drilling, thank goodness.
When I first heard the news, I was numbed by the shock.

The ravviſh danke of clumzie vvinter ramps / The fluent ſummers vaine: and drizling ſleete / Chilleth the vvan bleak cheek of the numd earth, / VVhilſt ſnarling guſts nibble the iuyceles leaues, / From the nak't ſhuddring branch; […]
But her main concern is the hard seating that numbs the nether regions.

glosses: To cause (a feeling) to be less intense.

examples.text: He turned to alcohol to numb his pain.
[I was] thankful for the pain, which helped to numb my terror.

glosses: To cause (the mind, faculties, etc.) to be less acute.

examples.text: […] hunger, fatigue, and despairing hopelessness had numbed his brain […]
The noise, the rush of air past our ears, was positively terrific. It actually seemed to numb the senses and make it almost impossible to take in impressions at all.
[The sofa] exhaled a breath of trapped ancient farts, barf-smell, and antiseptic, the parfum de asylum that gradually numbed my nose to all other scents on the ward.
[…] after fumbling with numbing fingers for ten or fifteen minutes, he waved his hand with a gesture of despair […]
[…] once more his feet began to numb. Again he got down and stamped the circulation going, but as soon as he began to ride again they numbed.

glosses: Having a thick edge or point; not sharp.

examples.text: The murderous knife was dull and blunt.

The dinghy was trailing astern at the end of its painter, and Merrion looked at it as he passed. He saw that it was a battered-looking affair of the prahm type, with a blunt snout, and like the parent ship, had recently been painted a vivid green.

The face which emerged was not reassuring. It was blunt and grey, the nose springing thick and flat from high on the frontal bone of the forehead, whilst his eyes were narrow slits of dark in a tight bandage of tissue. […].

glosses: Dull in understanding; slow of discernment; opposed to acute.

examples.text: His wits are not so blunt.

glosses: Abrupt in address; plain; unceremonious; wanting in the forms of civility; rough in manners or speech.

examples.text: I was taken aback by the blunt admission that he had never liked my company.
a plain, blunt man

December 30, 1736, Alexander Pope, letter to Jonathan Swift
I find my heart hardened and blunt to new impressions.

glosses: Slow or deficient in feeling: insensitive.
A fencer's practice foil with a soft tip.
A short needle with a strong point.

examples.text: […] to make his point, lead rapper B-Real fired up a blunt in front of the cameras and several hundred thousand people and announced, “I'm taking a hit for every one of y'all!”

glosses: Lacking the ability to cut easily; not sharp.

examples.text: All these knives are dull.

glosses: Not shiny; having a matte finish or no particular luster or brightness.

examples.text: Choose a dull finish to hide fingerprints.
a dull fire or lamp;  a dull red or yellow;  a dull mirror

glosses: Not bright or intelligent; stupid; having slow understanding.

examples.text: She is not bred so dull but she can learn.
dull at classical learning

glosses: Not intense; felt indistinctly or only slightly.

examples.text: Pressing on the bruise produces a dull pain.

glosses: Not clear, muffled. (of a noise or sound)

examples.text: Years of misuse have dulled the tools.

glosses: To soften, moderate or blunt; to make dull, stupid, or sluggish; to stupefy.

examples.text: He drinks to dull the pain.

glosses: To lose a sharp edge; to become dull.

examples.text: A razor will dull with use.

glosses: To render dim or obscure; to sully; to tarnish.
To make quiet or put at rest; to pacify or appease; to quell; to calm.

examples.text: to allay popular excitement
to allay the tumult of the passions
O love, be moderate, allay thy ecstacy, […]

glosses: To alleviate; to abate; to mitigate.

examples.text: to allay the severity of affliction or the bitterness of adversity
And the wynde alayed, and there folowed a greate calme: and he sayde unto them: why are ye fearfull?

For raging wind blows up incessant showers,
And when the rage allays the rain begins.

glosses: To mix (metals); to mix with a baser metal; to alloy; to deteriorate.
To make worse by the introduction of inferior elements.

examples.text: Yet far be it from us to condemn all their works to be dross, because debased and allayed with superstitious intents […]
